'Isa and al-Jahdari read *matwiyyatan* with the accusative, on the basis that *al-samawat* is conjoined to *al-ard*, sharing with it in the ruling, that is, "and the heavens are His handful." *Matwiyyatan* is a circumstantial clause relating to *al-samawat*, according to those who permit such a circumstantial clause coming from this kind of word, or relating to its hidden pronoun in *qabdatihi*, on the basis that it has the meaning of "grasped," or relating to its pronoun, omitted, that is, I establish them folded. *Wa-bi-yaminihi* (and in His right hand) is connected to *matwiyyatun*, or on the basis that *al-samawat* is the subject, *wa-bi-yaminihi* is the predicate, and *matwiyyatun* is a circumstantial clause as well, either relating to the subject, or to the omitted pronoun, or to the hidden pronoun in the predicate, on the basis of the view of al-Akhfash (a grammarian) that it is permissible to front a circumstantial clause in such a construction.

For many later scholars, the statement is an image portraying the state of His greatness, exalted is He, and the all-encompassing reach of His power, mighty and majestic is He, and the lowliness of the great acts at which imaginations are bewildered, when compared to the state of one who has a grasp in which is the whole earth and a right hand with which he folds the heavens. Or it is compared to the state of one who has a grasp in which are the earth and the heavens, and a right hand with which he folds the heavens, without moving the grasp or the right hand toward a direction, whether literal or figurative, in relation to what is attributed to Him, and He is Allah, great is His affair. Some said: the intention is to alert to the additional majesty of His glory, mighty and majestic is He, by conveying that the whole earth is under His dominion on the Day of Resurrection, so no other than He, exalted is His affair, disposes of it at all, as He, glorified is He, said:

﴿The dominion on that day belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 56]. *Wa-al-samawatu matwiyyatun* (and the heavens are folded up) like the folding of the scroll for the books, by His power which nothing can resist.

In it is an allusion that whatever they associate with Him, mighty and majestic is He, whether earthly or heavenly, is subdued under His authority, exalted is His majesty and mighty is His sovereignty. So the grasp is a metaphor for possession or disposal, as one says: "The town of such-and-such is in the grasp of so-and-so." The right hand is a metaphor for complete power. It has been said: the grasp is a metaphor for what has been mentioned and similar things, and by the right hand is meant the oath, that is, the heavens are annihilated by the cause of His oath, exalted is He, since He, mighty and majestic is He, swore to annihilate them. This is something to be mocked, not something to be cheered for its excellence. The early generation (*salaf*) also say: the statement is an alert to the additional majesty of His glory, exalted is He, and an allusion that their gods, whether earthly or heavenly, are subdued under His authority, mighty and majestic is He, except that they do not say that the grasp is a metaphor for possession or disposal, nor that the right hand is a metaphor for power. Rather, they declare Allah exalted above limbs and organs, and they affirm what He attributed to His essence in the sense He intended, glorified is He. They do the same with the reports transmitted on this point. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "A rabbi from among the rabbis came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Muhammad, we find that Allah carries the heavens on the Day of Resurrection on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and the moist earth on one finger, and the rest of creation on one finger, then He says: 'I am the King.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molars showed, confirming the words of the rabbi. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, recited: ﴿Nor have they measured God with His true measure﴾, the verse."

The interpreters (*al-mutawwilun*) interpret the fingers as power and ease, as in the saying of the speaker: "I kill Zayd with my finger." What is apparent in what Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it sound), al-Bayhaqi and others transmitted from Ibn Abbad (or Ibn 'Abbas, as in the text) distances this interpretation: "A Jew passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting, and said: 'How will you say, O Abu al-Qasim, when Allah places the heavens on this (finger)' and he pointed with the index finger, 'and the earths on this, and the mountains on this, and the rest of creation on this?' All of that he indicated with his fingers, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Nor have they measured God with His true measure﴾." Some interpreters made the gesture an aid to the image and imagination. Some claimed that the verse was revealed in refutation of the Jew, who likened God and went to anthropomorphism, and that the laughter of the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in the previous report was also a refutation, and that "confirming his words" in the report is from the words of the narrator, as he understood it. It is not hidden that this is very much contrary to the apparent sense. They also counted among the aids to the image and to the imagination of greatness the Prophet's ﷺ action when he recited this verse. Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and a group transmitted from Ibn Umar that "the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse one day on the pulpit: ﴿Nor have they measured God with His true measure, and the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾,
while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was saying, thus, with his hand, moving it, turning it over and back, 'The Lord glorifies Himself: I am the Mighty, I am the Proud, I am the King, I am the Mighty, I am the Generous.' And the pulpit shook beneath the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so much that we said: 'It will surely fall down with him.'"

In Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Muqsim, that he looked at Ibn Umar and saw how he related the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ words: "Allah, exalted is He, takes His heavens and His earths in His two hands and says: 'I am Allah,' and He grasps His fingers and extends them: 'I am the King.'"

In the commentary on Sahih Muslim by the Imam al-Nawawi, quoting al-Mazari, the Prophet's ﷺ grasping and extending his fingers is an image of the grasping of these created things and their gathering after they were spread out, and a narration of the spread-out and grasped thing, which is the heavens and the earths. It is not a reference to the grasping and extending which is an attribute of the One who grasps and extends, glorified and exalted is He, nor an image of God's auditory attribute called the hand, which is not a limb. End of quote. Then, the apparent sense of some reports requires that the grasping of the earth takes place after the folding of the heavens, and that it is with another hand.

Muslim transmitted from Ibn Umar, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah, exalted is He, will fold up the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, then He will take them in His right hand, then He says: I am the King; where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant? Then He will fold the earths with His left hand, then He says: Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?'"

In the commentary, also quoting al-Mazari: the ascription of two hands to God, exalted is He, is to be interpreted as power. It was expressed through two hands because our actions are done with two hands, so we are addressed in terms of what we understand, to be clearer and more firmly fixed in souls. He mentioned the right and the left so that the interpretation is complete, because with the right hand we take what we honour, and with the left what is less than that, and because in our case the right is stronger for what the left is not strong enough to bear. It is known that the heavens are greater than the earth, so He attributed them to the right hand and attributed the earths to the left, so that closeness appears in the metaphor, although God, exalted and glorified is He, is not described as having anything lighter or heavier for Him than another. End of quote.

The Sufis speak of the manifestation of form (*al-tajalli al-suwari*) while maintaining absoluteness (*al-itlaq*) and transcendence (*al-tanzih*), indicated by "There is nothing like unto Him" [al-Shura: 11]. The matter is very easy in this respect.

Then, the disposal of the earth and the heavens takes place while people are on the Path (*al-sirat*), as comes in a report narrated by Muslim from Aisha, traced to the Prophet ﷺ. It is also narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "On the Day of Resurrection the earth will be a single loaf, which the Mighty One will tip with His hand as one of you tips his loaf on a journey, as a provision for the people of Paradise." The discussion of this report is like the discussion of its counterparts. Beware of likening (*tashbih*) and anthropomorphism (*tajsim*), and likewise of attributing that to the early generation. Do not be like the Mu'tazilah in their bias against them and their slandering of them. The Mu'tazilah's ignorance of their Lord is sufficiently shown by their claim that He, mighty and majestic is He, delegated (*fawwada*) the servants, so they do what He does not will, and will what they do not do. ﴿Glorified is He, and exalted above what they associate﴾: that is, remove far from His association such a One whose power and greatness are such, or exalted above what they associate of partners. *Subhana* is for wonder, and *'an* is connected to it through the interpretation mentioned, and *ma* may be either verbal or relative.

[Page 28]

﴿And the Horn is blown﴾. It is well known that the one who blows it is a single angel, and that he is Israfil (peace be upon him). Indeed, al-Qurtubi reported a consensus (ijma') on this. However, there is a hadith narrated by Ibn Majah, al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, traced to the Prophet, that says: "The blowers are two." Other reports also indicate this. Among them is what Ahmad and al-Hakim narrated from Ibn Umar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The two blowers are in the second heaven. The head of one of them is in the east and his feet are in the west. They wait for the moment when they will be commanded to blow into the Horn, and so they blow." Some reports indicate that it is a single angel, and that he is gazing, i.e. Israfil (peace be upon him), who has not blinked since God created him, waiting until he is signalled, whereupon the Horn is blown. The Horn (al-Sur) is a great horn with holes in it, equal in number to every created spirit and every living soul. Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Wahb that it is made of a white pearl, clear like glass, with fine holes in it equal in number to the spirits, and in its middle is an opening as wide as the heavens and the earth. We believe in it and entrust its modality to the Knower of the unseen, exalted is His majesty.

Some have denied this and said: the word is the plural of ṣūrah (form), as in the reading of Qatadah and Zayd ibn Ali, "fi al-ṣuwar" with a fatḥah on the waw. The discussion of this has already passed. The verb is expressed in the past tense to affirm that the event has certainly occurred. The verb is put in the passive voice because the purpose does not depend on the agent; rather, the purpose is to convey the occurrence of this act from whichever agent it may be. It is as if it were said: "And the blowing into the Horn occurred." ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon﴾, i.e. they will die as a result of that. It is possible that they will first be overcome by unconsciousness and then die. In al-Asas it says: "A man swoons (ṣa'iqa) when he is overcome with unconsciousness from a crash or a loud sound he hears, and he dies (ṣa'iqa) when he dies."

In Sahih Muslim, from a long hadith which mentions the Dajjal: "Then the Horn will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he will incline his ear and raise his neck. The first to hear it will be a man who is mending the trough of his camels, and he will swoon, and the people will swoon." It has been read as "fa-ṣu'iqa" with a ḍammah on the ṣād. ﴿Except whom God wills﴾. Al-Suddi said: they are Jibril, Israfil, Mikail and the Angel of Death (peace be upon them all). It has also been said: they are these and the bearers of the Throne, for they will die afterwards. There is disagreement regarding the order of their deaths, as mentioned in al-Durr al-Manthur. It has been said: Ridwan, the houris, Malik and the Zabaniyah, and this was narrated from al-Dahhak. It has been said: those who died before that, i.e. whoever is in the heavens and the earth will die except those whose death has already preceded, because they had already died. In al-Bahr it says: "This is similar to ﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾ [al-Dukhan 44:56]." Among the strange opinions is what is reported that the one excepted is God, Mighty and Majestic. Your awareness of its condition is not hidden, whether the exception is connected (muttasil) or disconnected (munqati'). It has been said: it is Musa (peace be upon him), and the discussion of verifying this will come, God willing. Other opinions have been given.

By "the heavens" is meant, according to most opinions, the direction of height; otherwise the exception would not be connected, since the bearers of the Throne, for example, are not in the heavens in the known sense. It has been said: no sound report has come specifying them. ﴿Then it will be blown again﴾, i.e. into the Horn. This clearly indicates that it is not plural; otherwise it would have said "in them" with ﴿another﴾, i.e. another blowing. It indicates that the first mention, "and the Horn is blown," refers to a single blowing, as has been stated in several places, because the conjunction implies difference. If the absolute sense were intended, including the other blowing, there would be no point in mentioning it here. (﴿Another﴾) may be in the accusative, as an adjective of an implied verbal noun, i.e. "a blowing, another," or in the nominative, as an adjective of the deputy subject. On the first view, the deputy subject is the adverbial phrase.

It is authentically reported in the Sahihayn of al-Bukhari and Muslim that God sends down water from the heaven between the two blowings.

It has been reported in some narrations that it is like a light drizzle (ṭall, with the unpointed letter ṭā'), and in some it is like the semen of men, so that human bodies grow from it. Between the two blowings there are forty, and this is from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet. However, it does not specify what these forty are.

In a hadith narrated by Abu Dawud, they are forty years. Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Abd Allah ibn al-As, who said: "The first blowing is blown from the Eastern gate of Iliya' or he said the Western, and the second blowing from another gate, ﴿and then they are standing﴾, rising from their graves, ﴿looking﴾, i.e. waiting for what they are commanded, or waiting to see what will be done with them. It has been said: they will turn their eyes in all directions, like the gaze of one who is stupefied when a great calamity strikes him." It has been objected that their saying when they rise, ﴿Who has raised us from our resting place?﴾, is apparently at odds with this kind of gazing.

It is also permitted that "standing" (qiyam) means standing as opposed to moving, i.e. they will be stationary and motionless in their places, bewildered. It has been objected that God's saying ﴿And the Horn is blown, and behold, they rush out from the graves to their Lord﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:51] apparently contradicts this, because nasl means hastening in walking. Likewise His saying ﴿They will come out from the graves quickly, as if they were rushing to a target﴾ [al-Ma'arij 70:43]. Zayd ibn Ali read "qiyaman" with a fatḥah, so that the clause "they look" is their predicate, and "qiyaman" is an adverbial accusative of the pronoun in "they look", placed first for the sake of the rhyme; or it is an adverbial of the subject according to those who permit that. In al-Bahr it says: the accusative is an adverb of state, and the predicate of the subject is the adverbial phrase which is "idha" (the sudden "idha"), and it is a state which cannot be avoided, since it is the locus of benefit, unless the predicate is taken as omitted, i.e. "then they are resurrected or existing standing." If "qiyaman" is in the accusative as an adverb of state, then the governing element is that omitted predicate, if we accept it; otherwise the governing element is the one governing the adverbial phrase. If "idha" is an adverb of place, as appears to be required by the apparent sense of Sibawayh's statement, its implied sense is "then in the presence, they are standing." If it is an adverb of time, as Al-Rayashi held, its implied sense is "then at that time in which it was blown, they are", i.e. their existence. This added word is needed because an adverb of time cannot be a predicate about a body. If "idha" is a particle, as the Kufans claim, then the predicate must be supplied, unless we hold that "looking" is the predicate and it governs the adverb of state. End of quotation. By my life, the view of the Kufans is less strained.

Here there is a difficulty, based on the fact that they interpreted the blast of swooning as the first blowing, by which whoever remains on the face of the earth dies. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Imam Ahmad and others narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: "A man from the Jews in the market of Medina said: 'By Him who chose Musa above mankind!' A man from the Ansar raised his hand and slapped him. He said: 'Do you say this while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is among us?' I mentioned that to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: 'God, Exalted, said: ﴿And the Horn is blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they are standing, looking﴾. So I will be the first to raise his head, and behold, Musa is holding on to one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he raised his head before me, or whether he was among those whom God excepted.'" This contradicts interpreting the blast as that, because Musa (peace be upon him) died thousands of years before that blast. The possibility that he (peace be upon him) did not die, as has been said about al-Khidr and Ilyas, is something no living person should utter. As some eminent scholars said, this indicates that it is the blast of resurrection.

Al-Qadi Iyad said: it is possible that this is the swoon of terror after the raising, when the heavens are split, so the verses and the hadiths agree, and the blowings are three. This is the choice of Ibn al-Arabi. Al-Qurtubi refuted this, saying that Musa (peace be upon him) taking hold of a pillar of the Throne occurs only at the blast of resurrection, and he claimed that the correct view is that there are only two blowings, not three or four, as has been said.

Then he said: What removes the difficulty is what some of our shaykhs said: death is not pure non-existence with regard to the prophets (peace be upon them) and the martyrs, for they are existing, alive, even if we do not see them. When the blast of swooning is blown, everyone in the heavens and the earth swoons. The swooning of non-prophets is death, but the swooning of the prophets is unconsciousness. When the blast of resurrection is blown, whoever died is brought back to life, and whoever swooned regains consciousness. For this reason, it occurs in the Sahihayn: "I will be the first to regain consciousness." End of quotation. It is not hidden that this requires either saying that a homonym may be used in both its meanings at once, or resorting to general metaphor, or committing to the intention that they swooned, and that the death of those who die after the swoon is derived from another matter. So reflect.

[Page 30]

﴿And the earth shall shine﴾, i.e., the earth of the Gathering (al-Mahshar), which is the earth changed from the familiar earth. In the Sahih it is narrated: "People will be gathered on a white earth, pure and clean, like a loaf of fine bread, with no landmark on it for anyone." It is far more extensive than the familiar earth. In some narrations it is said: "On that day it will be of silver," but this is not authentic. I.e., it will shine ﴿with the light of its Lord﴾. According to what is narrated from Ibn Abbas, this is a light that Allah Most High creates without any luminous bodies such as the sun or moon. The Imam (al-Razi) chose this view and treated the idiomatic attribution (idafah) as in ﴿the she-camel of Allah﴾ [al-A'raf 73; Hud 64; al-Shams 13]. From Muhyi al-Sunnah (al-Baghawi), it is explained as the manifestation (tajalli) of the Lord for the decisive judgment. From al-Hasan and al-Suddi, it is explained as justice, and this is a usage of metaphor (isti'arah, a figure in which a word is used for something other than its literal meaning). This word has been used in this sense, as well as for the Qur'an and the proof (burhan), in several places in the Revelation. That is: the earth will shine with the truth and justice that He establishes in it, and with the equity (qist) He spreads, may He be glorified, in the reckoning and the weighing of good deeds and bad deeds. Al-Zamakhshari chose this view and first affirmed that metaphor by its recurrence in the Mighty Qur'an, then confirmed it secondly by his saying: "What points to this is the attribution to His name the Most High, because He, Mighty and Majestic, is the Truth, the Just, as an indication that turns away from the interpretive reading (ta'wil)." Thirdly, he made it consistent by attributing the name of His, the Most High, the Lord, to the earth, because justice is what the earth is adorned with, not proof, for example. Fourthly, by what is coordinated with the shining of the earth: the placing of the Book, the coming of the prophets and the witnesses, and the judgment with truth, because all of this is a detailing of justice in reality. Fifthly, he supported it by common custom, for people say to a just king: "The horizons have shone for you, and the world has been illuminated by your justice." Sixthly, by his (ﷺ) saying: "Injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection," for this requires that justice be light in it. Seventhly, by the fact that the opening and closing of the verse with the negation of injustice indicates this, so that it becomes an instance of returning the last part to the first in the manner of tard and 'aks (a rhetorical pattern of reversal). He preferred what the Imam had chosen, on the basis that the original sense is the literal meaning, and there is no reason to divert from it, because the idafah (attribution) is valid with the slightest connection. He supported what was reported from Muhyi al-Sunnah with some hadiths.

Sahib al-Kashf (the author of al-Kashf) commented on this, saying: "The attribution of connection (idafat al-mulabasah) is a figurative usage (majaz). Preference goes to what Jar Allah (al-Zamakhshari) chose, because of the benefits mentioned, and because it is the prevalent usage in the Qur'an. Do you not see His saying, Most High: ﴿Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Nur 35]? As for the manifestation (tajalli) of the Lord, glory be to Him, whether it is taken as the manifestation of majesty or the manifestation of beauty, it does not necessitate the earth shining with light, except in one of the two senses, namely justice, or an accident (ard) that Allah Most High creates at the manifestation in the earth. So if it were imagined that from His manifestation, may He be exalted, a light is reflected from Him onto the earth, that would be impossible except with the explanation mentioned. Therefore it is not a third view that can be supported and reinforced by the hadith, which does not indicate that it is an explanation of the verse; the hadith includes the hadith of the vision and the veiling of His screen over the servant, reminding him of what he did and what he committed." End of quotation. Perhaps the most suitable view, in line with what many reports suggest, is that His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿and the earth shall shine with the light of its Lord﴾ is an indication of His manifestation, Mighty and Majestic, for the decisive judgment, and this is sometimes expressed by "coming." He stated this in His saying, Most High: ﴿Will they wait until Allah comes to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels?﴾ [al-Baqarah 210]. The early generations (al-Salaf) did not interpret that; rather, they affirmed it for Him, glory be to Him, like descending, in the manner in which He affirmed it for Himself, Mighty and Majestic.

It is not far-fetched that this light is the light mentioned in the authentic hadith: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, nor is it fitting for Him to sleep; He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light." It may be said of it, as of a veil, in the manner the early generations said regarding the rest of the ambiguous (mutashabihat) matters. Or it is another light that appears at that manifestation. I do not say that it is a light reflected from the Sacred Essence like the reflection of sunlight from the sun, for example; rather, the matter is beyond what minds reach. How, when, and where could one conceive of the reality of that arrival? The use of the title of Lordship (al-Rububiyyah), attributed to the pronoun of the earth, points to the fact that this manifestation is linked with justice. And Allah Most High knows best what He intends.

Ibn Abbas, Ubayd ibn Umayr and Abu al-Jawza' read ﴿أشْرَقَتْ﴾ in the passive form (ashraqat, with the passive voice). Al-Zamakhshari said: it comes from shariqat bi-al-daw' (شَرِقَتْ بِالضَّوْءِ), which means "to become full of it and saturated," and Allah Most High illuminated it (ashraqaha), just as you say: "He filled the earth with justice and covered it with justice." Ibn Atiyyah said: "This only follows from a verb that is transitive. So this is on the basis that one says: ashraqa al-bayt (أشرق البيت), and ashraqahu al-siraj (أشرقه السراج), so the verb is both transitive and intransitive." The author of al-Lawami' said: "On this reading, the meaning of ishraq must necessarily be transferred from shariqat al-shams (شرقت الشمس), when the sun rises, so that it becomes transitive, and the meaning is: it removed the darkness of the earth. It cannot be from ashraqat (أشرقت), when it shines, for that is intransitive, although this may be transitive to an object."

﴿And the Book will be placed﴾. Al-Suddi said: "The reckoning." So "the Book" is a metaphor for the reckoning, and its placing is an elaboration of it, and what is meant by it is the beginning of it. It is also permissible to take the statement as an illustration (tamthil, a figure of speech depicting a scene).

Some said: "The records of deeds were placed in the hands of the recording angels." So the definite article is for the genus or for totality. It was said: "The Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) was placed so that the records might be compared with it," so the definite article is for a specific referent. This view was narrated from Ibn Abbas, but Abu Hayyan considered it unlikely and said: "Perhaps it is not authentic from Ibn Abbas."

﴿And the prophets will be brought﴾. It was said: "So that they may be asked whether they conveyed to their nations," and it was said: "So that they may attend their reckoning."

﴿And the witnesses﴾. Ata, Muqatil and Ibn Zayd said: "The guardian angels (al-hafazah)." It is as if they intended that they bear witness for each of the nations that they were conveyed to, or that they bear witness concerning each person regarding his deeds, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And every soul will come with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf 21].

In some reports it is said that the Preserved Tablet will be brought while trembling, and it will be said to it: "Did you convey to Israfil?" It will say: "Yes, my Lord, I conveyed to him." Then Israfil will be brought, trembling, and it will be said to him: "Did the Tablet convey to you?" He will say: "Yes, my Lord." At that point the fear of the Tablet will subside. Then it will be said to Israfil: "And you, did you convey to Jibril?" He will say: "Yes, my Lord." Then Jibril will be brought, trembling, and it will be said to him: "Did Israfil convey to you?" He will say: "Yes, my Lord." At that point the fear of Israfil will subside. Then it will be said to Jibril: "And you, did you convey?" He will say: "Yes, my Lord." Then the messengers will be brought, trembling, and it will be said to them: "Did Jibril convey to you?"

They will say: "Yes." At that point the fear of Jibril will subside. Then it will be said to them: "And you, did you convey?" They will say: "Yes." Then it will be said to the nations: "Did the messengers convey to you?" Their disbelievers will say: "No bearer of good news nor warner came to us." The situation will become grievous for the messengers, and their anguish will intensify. Then it will be said to them: "Who will testify for you?" They will say: "The unlettered Prophet and his community." So the Muhammadan community will be brought, and they will testify that the messengers conveyed. Then it will be said to them: "From where do you know that?" They will say: "From a Book Allah Most High revealed to us, in which He, glory be to Him, mentioned that the messengers conveyed to their nations, and the Prophet (ﷺ) vouches for them." That is His saying, Most High: ﴿Thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah 143]. From here it was said: the intended witnesses in the verse are the community of our Prophet (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him).

Al-Jubba'i and Abu Muslim said: they are the upright ('udul) of the Hereafter, who bear witness for the nations and against them. It was said: all witnesses are intended, from the angels, the community of Muhammad (peace be upon him), the limbs, and the place. Whatever the case, "the witnesses" is the plural of "witness" (shahid). Qatadah and al-Suddi said: the intended are those who were martyred in the way of Allah, so it is the plural of "martyr" (shahid), but this is not the case.

﴿And judgment will be made between them﴾, i.e., between the servants, as is understood from the context, ﴿with truth﴾, i.e., with justice, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, i.e., by a diminution of reward or an increase of punishment in accordance with what the promise has determined. This is based on the premise that injustice in reality is inconceivable with respect to Him, Most High, for the whole matter belongs to Him, Mighty and Majestic.

And every soul will be paid in full for what it did (i.e., it will be given its recompense completely), ﴿and He is most knowing of what they do﴾, so nothing of their deeds escapes Him, glorified is He.

The verbal noun, "And their being driven..." (﴿وسِيقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إلى جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًا﴾ .. إلخ), is an elaboration of the "tawfiyah" (full recompense, the complete repayment of deeds) and an explanation of how it occurs. The fa' (so) is not obligatory here. "Sawq" (driving) implies urging to walk with violence and harassment, which is its usual sense, and it suggests humiliation, which is what is meant here. That is, they are driven to it with violence and humiliation, in groups (afwaj) scattered, one following another, arranged according to the order of their ranks in misguidance and wickedness.

[Page 32]

"Zumar" is the plural of "zumrah" (a group). Al-Raghib said: it is a small group. From this comes the saying "shatun zumrah" (a goat with little hair) and "rajulun zumr" (a man of little manliness). From the same root is derived "al-zamr" (playing a wind instrument), and "al-zammarah" is a metaphorical term for a immoral woman. Some have said: the derivation of "zumrah" is from "al-zamr," which is a sound, since a group is never free of sound.

﴿حَتّى إذا جاءُوها فُتِحَتْ أبْوابُها﴾ (until, when they come to it, its gates are opened) so that they may enter it. Before their arrival, its gates were not open. It is like the gates of prisons, which remain closed until the people of crimes who are to be imprisoned in them arrive; then they are opened so that they may enter. When they have entered, they are locked upon them. "Hatta" (until) here is the particle after which a sentence is narrated, and the discussion of "idhā" (when) occurring after it has already passed in Surat al-An'am. Several readers read "futtiḥat" with the doubled letter (intensive form).

﴿وقالَ لَهم خَزَنَتُها﴾ (And its keepers will say to them) as a rebuke and reproach. ﴿ألَمْ يَأْتِكم رُسُلٌ مِنكُمْ﴾ (Did there not come to you messengers from among you?), that is, of your own kind, whom you understand in what they tell you, and whom it is easy for you to consult.

Ibn Harmuz read "ta'tikum" with the feminine ta' (ta' al-ta'nith). It is also read "nudhurun minkum" (warners from among you).

﴿يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْكم آياتِ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ (who recite to you the signs of your Lord) which were revealed for your benefit, ﴿ويُنْذِرُونَكم لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ﴾ (and warn you of the meeting of this your day), that is, this time of yours, which is the time of your entry into the Fire, because what is warned of in reality is the punishment and its time. It is also permitted that what is meant by it is the Day of Resurrection and the Hereafter, since it includes this time, or what is specific to them of its punishment and terrors. Its being in itself not specific to them does not contradict this, and the idafah (genitive construction) here is of the lam type, which indicates specificity, because what has been mentioned is sufficient for specificity. Yes, the first interpretation is more apparent in it.

The verse has been cited as evidence that there is no obligation (taklif) before the Law (shar'), because they rebuke them for their disbelief after the messengers had conveyed the laws and warned them. If the ugliness of disbelief were known by reason without revelation, it would have been said: "Did you not know, by what God Most High placed within you of intellect, the ugliness of your disbelief?" There is no basis for interpreting "the messengers" as "the intellects," because the actions attributed to them refuse that. Yes, it is a persuasive proof (dalil iqna'i), since it is complete only on the basis of considering the concept of implication (mafhum) and the generality of "those who disbelieved," and both of these are matters of dispute. It has been said regarding the manner of inferring from it: the address to those who enter is in general, which requires that all of them were warned by the messengers. Had there been an obligation before the Law, the matter would not be so. It has been objected to that the opponent may not accept the generality, and that one who holds that faith is obligatory by reason may say: they rebuked them for disbelief after conveying the message, because that is further from excuse and more deserving of rebuke and denunciation.

﴿قالُوا بَلى﴾ (They will say: Yes), indeed there came to us messengers from among us who recited to us the signs of our Lord and warned us of the meeting of this our day. ﴿ولَكِنْ حَقَّتْ﴾ (But the word has become due), that is, it became obligatory, ﴿كَلِمَةُ العَذابِ﴾ (the word of punishment), that is, the word of God Most High which necessitates it, ﴿عَلى الكافِرِينَ﴾ (against the disbelievers). What is meant by it is the judgment against them of wretchedness, and that they are among the people of the Fire because of their wrong choice; or it is the saying of God Most High to Iblis: ﴿لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ ومِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ (I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all together) [Sad 38:85]. They placed "the disbelievers" in the place of their pronoun, to indicate the exalted status of disbelief. The statement is a confession, not an excuse.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 39, verse 72:

﴿It was said: "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein."﴾ That is, your abiding therein is decreed. The one who says this may be the guardians (al-Khazanah) and their mention was omitted because they are known from what precedes. It may also be someone other than them, and he was not mentioned because the intent is to convey this awesome statement itself, without regard to who said it. Some of the eminent scholars said: the speaker is left unspecified in order to magnify what is said.

﴿So evil is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ The alif-lam (al) in al-mutakabbirin, whether it is the definite article or the relative pronoun for the class, serves to supply the required agent (fa'il) for the verbal form ni'ma and bi'sa (the verbs of praise and blame). The item being blamed (al-makhsus bil-dhamm) is omitted, relying on its mention just before, so the meaning is: "so evil is their abode, Hell." The expression "abode" (al-mathwa) corresponds to "abiding" (khalidin). In the expression "the arrogant" there is a hint that their entry into the Fire was because of their arrogance in refusing to accept the truth and submit to the messengers who warned them, peace be upon them; this has the sense of giving the reason as disbelief. This does not conflict with ascribing it to the prior certainty of the word of punishment against them, because His, exalted is He, judgment and decree concerning them to enter the Fire is nothing other than because of their arrogance and disbelief, due to their bad choice, which was known to Him, glorified is He, from eternity. Likewise is His, mighty and majestic is He, saying: "I will surely fill [Hell]." So there are two causes, a near one and a distant one, and giving the reason by one of them does not negate giving it by the other. So reflect and ponder.

[Page 33 continues from the earlier text]

﴿And those who had feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups﴾ — groups arranged in order according to the ranks of their stations in virtue. In the Sahih of Muslim and others, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The first group of my community to enter the Garden will be in the likeness of the moon on the night of the full moon. Then those who follow them will be like the brightest star in the sky. After that they will be in various levels.'" The meaning of "driving" (al-sawq) here is urging them to hasten toward honour. This is unlike its use earlier, where it is for the humiliation of the disbelievers and hastening them to punishment and pain. It was chosen for the sake of mushakalah (correspondence in wording, i.e., matching the same verb to contrasting situations). His saying, glorified is He, ﴿to the Garden﴾ removes the suggestion of humiliation. Yet it may be said that when they loved meeting Allah, the Exalted, Allah loved meeting them, and so they were urged to enter the abode of His honour, may His majesty be exalted. This was said by some of the eminent scholars.

Al-Zamakhshari chose that the intended meaning of their "driving" here is the driving of their mounts, since they are not taken [to the Garden] except riding. This driving and urging is also for hastening them to the abode of honour.

This has been criticised: there is no indication that this is intended, and that all the God-fearing are taken only while riding requires proof. The argument from His saying, exalted is He, ﴿On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾ [Maryam: 85] is only valid if one holds that delegations are only riders, and that riding continues for them until they enter the Garden. In al-Kashf, it is said that this is an apparent interpretation, supported by numerous hadiths, and suited to the context, because the two drivings come after the judgment is concluded: pure kindness toward some and pure subjugation toward others. It does not contradict the station of the majesty of the King of kings, contrary to what has been imagined. End.

I say: if "those who had feared" is taken to mean the sincere ones (al-mukhlisin), then the view of their riding is a strong view. If it is taken to mean only those who guard against shirk, to include the sincere ones, then that view is weak, since among them are those who do not enter the Garden until they first enter the Fire and are punished therein. The apparent meaning of many reports is that among this category are those who go to the Garden on foot.

In the Sahih of Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The last person to enter the Garden is a man who walks, sometimes stumbling and sometimes being scorched by the Fire. When he passes it, he turns toward it and says, 'Blessed is He who saved me from you! Allah has given me something He has given no one else among the first or the last.' Then a tree is raised for him, and he says, 'My Lord, bring me near this tree so that I may shade myself under its shade and drink from its water.' Allah says, 'O son of Adam, perhaps if I give you it, you will ask Me for something else.' He says, 'No, my Lord,' and he pledges that he will not ask Him for anything else. His Lord excuses him, because He sees what he cannot bear to be without, so He brings him near." [The hadith continues.]

Some of the knowers of Allah said: the God-fearing are driven to the Garden because they saw Allah, the Exalted, in the place of gathering. Out of their desire to see Him, mighty and majestic, a second time, they do not like to leave that station where they saw Him. And because of the intensity of their love and their ardour, it hardly occurs to them that they will see Him, glorified is He, when they enter the Garden. When love is great, it does to its possessor something greater than that, and greater still. It overcomes them until it seems to them that that place is the place where they will see Him, mighty and majestic, and it is the place of His self-manifestation to His lovers, exalted is His majesty and great is His bounty. So they hold back from walking and stand waiting to see the Subtle, the All-Aware. And the tongue of each of them, in the state of his heart, came to say:

*The longing halted me where you are, so I have no one who is behind it, nor one who goes ahead of it.*

And what indicates their seeing Him, mighty and majestic, there is what is in the Sahih of Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Some people said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), 'O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon?' They said, 'No, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun when there is no cloud beneath it?' They said, 'No.' He said:

[Page 34]

'Indeed, you will see Him in the same way. Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection and say: whoever used to worship anything should follow it. So whoever worshipped the sun will follow the sun, whoever worshipped the moon will follow the moon, and whoever worshipped the false deities will follow the false deities. This community will remain, including its hypocrites. Then Allah, blessed and exalted is He, will come to them in a form other than the one they recognise, and He will say, "I am your Lord." They will say, "We seek refuge in Allah from You. This is our place until our Lord comes to us. When our Lord comes, we will recognise Him." Then Allah will come to them in His form which they recognise, and He will say, "I am your Lord." They will say, "You are our Lord," and they will follow Him. The Sirat will be set up between the backs of Hell. I and my community will be the first to cross it. On that day, none will speak except the Messengers, and the Messengers' call on that day will be, "O Allah, grant safety, grant safety."'" [The hadith continues.]

Yet, with all this, their driving is not like the driving of those who disbelieved, as is not hidden.

It has been said: the driver of the disbelievers is the angels of wrath, and the driver of the God-fearing is their longing for their Master. He, glorified is He, is for them the ultimate object of their desire. The Garden is not, in their view, the goal in itself, nor merely dwelling in it the supreme pleasure. Rather, it is a means to meeting their Beloved, who is the ultimate goal of their quest. ﴿Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾. It is also read with the doubled consonant (shaddah) on the letter fa'. The waw is for the circumstantial clause, and the clause is in the circumstantial position with "qad" implied, according to the well-known view: that is, they reach it, and its gates have already been opened for them, as in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Gardens of Eden, their gates opened for them﴾ [Sad: 50]. This indicates that the opening came first, as though the keepers of the Gardens had opened its gates and stood waiting for them. This is like servants opening the door of a house for a guest invited to a feast before he arrives, and standing waiting for him. There is in that much honour and respect.

The apparent view is that His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And its keepers will say to them﴾ … etc., is coordinated with "its gates were opened." The answer to "when" (idha) is omitted and implied after "abiding," to indicate that for them, at that time, there are kinds of honour which speech cannot encompass. As if it were said: "When they reach it with its gates opened for them, and its keepers say to them: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾," that is, from all disliked things and pains. This may be either a report or a greeting.

﴿You are good﴾, that is, pure from the filth of sins. It was said: "You are good" means you are content with what has been granted to you of lasting bliss. The first is related from Mujahid and is the more apparent. The clause is in the position of causation: ﴿So enter it, abiding forever﴾, that is, intending to abide forever, whatever it is, of what cannot be described fully, or you have attained what cannot be counted or measured of honour and exaltation. Al-Mubarrad estimated it as "you are happy" after "abiding" also. Some estimated it before "and its gates were opened," meaning "until, when they reach it, they reach it when its gates are opened," but this is nothing. Some estimated it in a manner similar to what we have said, before "and [its keepers] said," and made the clause "said…" coordinated with it. What was mentioned earlier is stronger in meaning and clearer.

The Kufans said: the waw in "and its gates were opened" is superfluous, and the answer is the clause "its gates were opened." It was also said: the answer is "its keepers said to them," and the waw is superfluous. What we mentioned first is the reliable view. By it, the reason for the difference between the two clauses becomes known: His saying, exalted is He, about the people of the Fire, ﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates are opened﴾, and His saying, glory to His majesty, about the people of the Garden, ﴿Until, when they reach it, and its gates are opened﴾. Here a waw is used in the second clause and the answer is omitted, whereas this is not done in the first clause. As for what has been said, that the waw in the second is the "waw of eight" (waw al-thamaniyah), because the opened gates are eight while the gates of Hell are seven and not eight, so the waw was not used for it, this is a weak view which is not relied upon.

The Mu'tazilah used as evidence His saying, ﴿You are good, so enter it﴾, since in it the command to enter is ordered upon goodness and purity from the filth of sins, from which it follows that no one enters the Garden except one who is good and pure from sins, either because he did not commit any of them or because he repented from what he did in a repentance accepted in this world. It was answered that although this shows that no one enters it except one who is good, that may be achieved through accepted repentance, or through His pardon, or intercession for him, or after he is purified by punishment. So there is no basis in it for the Mu'tazilah.

[Page 35]

It was said: the intended meaning of "those who had feared" is those who guard specifically against shirk. So "You are good" means you are pure from the filth of shirk. There is no disagreement that entering the Garden is caused by goodness and purity from it. It was criticised: this is contrary to the apparent meaning, because taqwa (God-consciousness, fear) in common usage falls upon something more specific than that, especially in a context of praise and in what follows it, His saying, exalted is He, ﴿How excellent is the reward of the doers﴾. So reflect.

**Ruh al-Ma'ani of al-Alusi, on surah 39, verse 74:**

﴿And they will say﴾ is coordinated (*ʿaṭf*, conjunction) with "said" (*qāla*), or with the implied answer after "abiding therein" (*khālidīn*), or with some other implied element, meaning: they entered it and said: ﴿Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾ regarding the resurrection and the reward, ﴿and has made us inherit the earth﴾. They mean the place in which they have settled. If the earth of the Hereafter on which they walk is called "earth" in the literal sense, then that is so. Otherwise, their use of "earth" for that place is by way of metaphor (*istiʿāra*), likening it to the earth of this world. The first is the more apparent meaning. It is reported from Qatada, Ibn Zayd and al-Suddi that the intended meaning is the earth of this world, but this is not correct. The "inheritance" of it means its being given to them as ownership, with what remains of it left to them from their deeds, or their being empowered to dispose of it in the manner an heir is empowered over what he inherits. This is based on the principle that there is no ownership in the Hereafter for anyone other than Him, Mighty and Majestic. Rather, it is only permission to dispose of and be empowered over what is His possession, exalted is His majesty. It has also been said: they inherited it from the people of the Fire, since each of them has a place in Paradise that was written for him on condition of faith.

﴿We settle in Paradise wherever we wish﴾: that is, each of us settles in whatever place he desires within His vast Paradise. It does not mean that each of them settles in any place within Paradise in general, or within the gardens of others that are designated for those others. Thus it cannot be objected that this would imply that all of them could settle in one single place as a literal unity, which is impossible, or that one of them could take the garden of another, which is not intended. It has also been said that the statement is on its apparent meaning: each of them may settle in whatever place he wills within Paradise in general and within the gardens of others, except that he does not will any place other than his own, owing to the soundness of his self and God's protection of him from such a wish. The Imam said: The philosophers of Islam have said that each (person) has two gardens, a physical one and a spiritual one, and the stations of the second do not obstruct one another. Thus it is possible that in one station of it there may be an unlimited number of its inhabitants. This clause is circumstantial (*ḥāl*), so the meaning is: He made us inherit the stations of Paradise, while we roam through the dwellings of the spirits as we wish.

One of the divine philosophers (*mutaʾallihī al-ḥukamāʾ*) has said: a narrow abode can contain a million million spirits and ideal forms, which are the bodies of those detached from elemental bodies, because they do not obstruct one another, as it has been said:

*"The eye of the needle, with the beloved, is a vast arena."*

The spiritual station has been explained as that which the spirit perceives of divine knowledge and witnesses of God's good pleasure and His sacred care, "such as no eye has seen, nor ear has heard."

It has been objected that if this is counted among the inner meanings (*buṭūn*) of the Great Qur'an, then there is no dispute; otherwise, interpreting "Paradise" in this manner is something the Arabs would not recognize, and it should not be used to explain it. Moreover, it may be said that it entails that every person can attain a spiritual station of it, although some of its stations are specific to the honoured prophets and the near angels. The apparent meaning is that not every one of the knowers can attain their stations. So understand this, and do not be heedless.

﴿How excellent is the reward of those who act﴾: according to most scholars, this is part of the speech of those who enter (Paradise). The object of the praise is omitted, meaning: this reward, or Paradise. Perhaps the expression "the reward of those who act" rather than "our reward" is to imply, by allusion, that the people of the Fire are not doers. Muqatil said: it is part of the speech of God, Exalted.

[p. 36]

Ibn 'Abbas's commentary and the verse: "And you see the angels surrounding (ḥāffīn)," meaning encircling, from *al-ḥiffāf*, which means the side. It is the plural of *ḥāff*, as al-Akhfash said. Al-Farra' said that it is not used in the singular. It was said that he meant that the singular cannot be *ḥāff*, since encircling and surrounding cannot be conceived of in a single individual and can only be realized through a plurality. It was also said that he meant that the singular form has not been attested in usage.

An objection to the first view is that surrounding something means facing all of its sides. This can be conceived of in a single individual by his revolving around the thing, since he then faces all its sides gradually. So *ḥufūf* (encircling) would mean revolving around it. Or it may be meant that by being *ḥāff* he is a part of the encircling group and has a share in the encircling. If what was mentioned were correct, one could not say *ṭā'if* (circumambulating), *muḥdiq* (encircling), *muḥīṭ* (surrounding), or similar words that indicate surrounding.

An objection to the second view is that we do not find a sound plural whose singular has not been attested. So after the occurrence of *ḥāffīn*, the apparent expectation is that *ḥāff* occurs, as is not hidden.

The address is to the master of the addressed, may Allah bless him and grant him peace (ﷺ). It is also permitted that it be addressed to everyone who is capable of seeing, as if it were said: "And you, O seer, see the angels surrounding **[the Throne from around the Throne]**." That is, around the Throne, on the view that *min* is superfluous according to al-Akhfash, and this is the most apparent view. It was also said that *min* is for the starting point, so "around the Throne" is the starting point of the encircling, and the encircling is then for the creatures. Some reports contain something that expresses this. Among them is what indicates that on the Day of the Decisive Judgment the Throne will be in the earth wherever Allah the Exalted wills, and the earth on that day will be other than this earth. However, the conditions of the Day of Resurrection and the affairs of Allah the Exalted are beyond our intellects, and glory be to the One whom nothing can overpower.

The apparent view is that the seeing is visual. Then *ḥāffīn* is the first circumstantial clause. The Exalted's saying, **"glorifying the praise of their Lord,"** is the second circumstantial clause. It is also permitted that it be a circumstantial clause from the concealed pronoun in *ḥāffīn*. It is permitted that the seeing be cognitive, with *ḥāffīn* as the second object, and the clause "they glorify" is a circumstantial clause from "the angels" or from their pronoun in *ḥāffīn*. The *bā'* in "with the praise" indicates accompaniment, and the prepositional phrase is in the position of a circumstance. That is, they exalt Him, the Exalted, above what does not befit Him, while accompanied by His praise. The summary is that they mention Allah the Exalted with the two attributes of His majesty and His generosity, may He be blessed and exalted. This mention is either from the category of delight, for mentioning the beloved is among the greatest pleasures of the lover, as it has been said:

*I find blame for Your sake to be sweet,*
*Love for the mention of You; so let the blamers blame me.*

Or it is from the category of obedience, and it is claimed that they are under obligation. It is not granted that they are outside the scope of obligation, or that they will leave it on the Day of Resurrection. Yes, they do not regard it as a burden, even if they are commanded to do it.

In a very long hadith, which 'Abd ibn Humayd and 'Ali ibn Sa'id reported in *Kitāb al-Ṭā'a wa al-'Iṣyān*, and Abu Ya'la and Abu al-Hasan al-Qattan reported in the lengthy compilations, and Abu al-Shaykh reported in *al-'Aẓama*, and al-Bayhaqi reported in *al-Ba'th wa al-Nushūr*, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: "While we are standing – that is, in the place of gathering – we hear a very loud sound from the sky, and the people of the lowest heaven descend, twice the number of those on the earth from the jinn and mankind. When they approach the earth, the earth becomes illuminated by their light, and they take their ranks. Then the people of the third heaven descend, twice the number of those who descended of the angels and twice the number of those in it of the jinn and mankind. When they approach the earth, the earth becomes illuminated by their light, and they take their ranks. Then they descend according to that multiplication up to the seven heavens. Then the Almighty descends in shadows of clouds, and the angels carry His Throne on that day, eight of them, while today they are four. Their feet are on the lowest boundaries of the earth, and the earths and the heavens reach their waists, and the Throne is on their shoulders. They have a chanting with glorification, and they say: 'Glory be to the Possessor of might and majesty. Glory be to the Possessor of dominion and sovereignty. Glory be to the Living who does not die. Glory be to the One who causes creatures to die and does not die. Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of the angels and the Spirit. Glory be to our Lord, the Most High, who causes creatures to die and does not die.' Then He places His Throne wherever He wills on the earth. Then He, glorified be He, calls out with His voice, and the Mighty and Majestic says: 'O assembly of jinn and mankind, I have been silent toward you since the day I created you until this day of yours. I hear your speech and I see your deeds. So listen to Me, for these are only your deeds and your records, which are being read to you. Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah the Exalted, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame none but himself.'" The hadith continues.

[p. 37]

**"And judgment is passed between them with truth."** That is, among all the servants, by admitting some of them to Paradise and some of them to Hellfire, for the known judgment takes place among them. Because this is clear, it does not harm that the pronoun refers to other than the angels, while the pronoun in "they glorify" refers to them, since separating the pronouns is not absolutely prohibited, as is imagined. It was said that the pronoun in "between them" refers to the angels, and Abu Hayyan preferred this. Their reward, although they are all infallible, follows the degrees of their deeds, so the differences in their ranks vary. Thus, placing each one in his station according to his deed is the judgment between them with truth.

**"And it is said: Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds."** That is, for what He judged between us with truth. The one who says "it is said" is the believers for whom judgment was passed, not those who include them and those against whom judgment was passed. Their first praise is for the fulfilment of His promise, may He be glorified, and the giving of the earth to them, so that they settle in Paradise wherever they wish. This praise of theirs is for the judgment with truth between them, so there is no repetition.

Al-Ṭībī said: The first is for the separation between the two groups according to promise and threat, and wrath and good pleasure. The second is for the distinction between them according to the bodies, so one group is in Paradise and another group is in the blaze. The first is better. It was also said that they are the angels, praising Him, the Exalted, for His judgment, glorified be He, between them with truth and for placing each of them in his station. According to this, there is no trace of repetition in the two praises, because the praisers differ.

It was also said: "it is said" rather than "they said," because of their identification and glorification. It is also permitted that the speaker be all the servants, the blessed and the punished. It seems that the praise is meant to come from the general creation, who are judged between them here, as an indication of completion and the end of disputes, as those leaving a session of a court or the like say. The believers praise Him because their right has become manifest, and others praise Him for His justice and for their relief from waiting for the decision. In some reports, the standing in the place of gathering is prolonged for the servants, to the extent that one of them says: "Lord, give me rest, even if it is to the Fire." It was also said that they praise Him to express contentment and submission.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This praise is a conclusion of the matter, said at the end of the decisive judgment, meaning that this just Judge should be praised when His ruling takes effect and His judgment is completed. From this verse, "Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds" was made the closing of gatherings of knowledge. This, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and His blessings and peace upon His messenger Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, and upon his family and all his companions.

* * *

**[From the path of allusion in some verses]** **"So worship Allah, making religion sincerely His."** That is, worship Him, the Exalted, with your self, heart, and spirit, sincerely. Sincerity of worship with the self is distance from deficiency; sincerity of worship with the heart is blindness to the sight of individuals; and sincerity of worship with the spirit is negation of seeking distinction. It has been mentioned that the sincere one is the one who is purified by generosity from detaining existence. **"Indeed Allah does not guide one who is a liar, an ungrateful disbeliever."** In this is an allusion to the threat against one who claims a rank of sainthood without being truthful in it, and his punishment is deprivation of that rank. **"He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night."** In this is an allusion to the states of those traveling to Allah, glorified be He: contraction and expansion, sobriety and intoxication, gathering and separation, veiling and manifestation, and other things. **"In three darknesses."** It was said: it alludes to the darkness of possibility, the darkness of matter, and the darkness of form. **"Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing?"** It alludes to upholding the etiquettes of servanthood outwardly and inwardly without slackness or shortcoming. **"Fearing the Hereafter"** and its bliss, just as he fears this world and its adornment. **"And hoping for the mercy of his Lord"** – His good pleasure, glorified be He, with him, and His nearness, the Mighty and Majestic. **"Say: Are those who know"** the measure of their Worshipped One, may His majesty be exalted, so they seek Him, **"equal to those who do not know,"** that, so they seek other than Him? **"Only those of understanding remember"** the reality of the matter. **"Those of understanding"** are those who have stripped off the skin of their existence and purified themselves of the impurities of their egoism. **"Say: O My servants who have believed"** in Me, longing for Me, **"fear your Lord,"** so do not seek other than Him, glorified be He. **"For those who do good"** in seeking Me in this world, by not seeking from Me other than Me, **[there is a good (ḥasana)]** great, which is the good of finding Me. **"And Allah's earth is spacious"** – it is the presence of His majesty and beauty, for it has no end. So let him travel through it to see what he sees, and let him not think, regarding what has been opened to him, that the journey has ended and the outpouring has ceased. **"Only the patient will be paid their reward"** for the sincerity of seeking, **"their reward,"** from the manifestations, **"without reckoning,"** since there is no end to His manifestations, the Exalted. **"Every day He is in a matter"** [Ar-Rahman: 29]. **"Say: Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord,"** by seeking other than Him, **"the punishment of a tremendous day."** It is the punishment of severance and deprivation. **"Say: Allah I worship, making my religion sincerely His."** So I seek neither this world nor the Hereafter, as it has been said:

*Each has a request, a religion, and a path,*
*and for me you are my request and my religion, your love.*

**"Say: Indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves"** – that is, those whose loss of their selves has become evident by corrupting their readiness to reach and to union, **"and their families"** – from the hearts, secrets, and spirits – by turning away from seeking the Master, **"on the Day of Resurrection,"** the day on which realities become manifest. **"That is the manifest loss,"** in which there is no hiding, because the capital is lost and recovery is impossible.

Some eminent scholars said: A human being has two powers, by one of which he perfects knowledge and by the other action. The instrument that intermediates in the first category is the sciences called the premises, and arranging them in the manner that leads to conclusions, which are like profit, resembles a merchant's dealing with capital through buying and selling. The instrument in the practical category is the bodily powers and other external means that assist them. Using those powers in the aspects of righteous deeds, which are like profit, resembles trade. Whoever Allah the Exalted has given reason, health, and capacity, then he has not benefited from them the knowledge of the Truth or the practice of good, when he dies his profit is lost, his capital is wasted, and he falls into the punishment of ignorance and the pain of distance from his world and nearness to what opposes it forever and ever. There is no loss beyond this and no deprivation clearer than it. Glorified be He, indicated this by His saying, the Exalted: **"For them there will be layers of fire above them and layers below them."** On the first view, this is an allusion to the fire of regret encompassing them. **"But those who feared their Lord will have chambers above which are built chambers, beneath which rivers flow."** It was said that the built chambers, some above others, are an allusion to acquired knowledge built upon theories, and that it is in firmness and certainty like innate, self-evident knowledge. **"Have you not seen that Allah sent down water from the sky"** – from the sky of His presence, glorified be He, or from the sky of the heart – water, the water of gnosis and knowledge. **"And caused it to flow as springs"** – faculties and powers – **"in the earth"** – the earth of humanity. **"Then He brings out by it crops"** – of bodily deeds and tongue-words. **"Then it dries up, and you see it turning yellow; then He makes it into debris."** This is an allusion to the deeds and words of the showy: they are seen green in accordance with the Law, then they turn yellow from the blight of showing off, then they become debris with no benefit in them except regret. **"Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam"** – to submission to Him, glorified be He – **"so that he is upon light from his Lord"** – illuminated by it in seeking Him, glorified be He. Among the signs of this light is the erasure of the darknesses of blameworthy soul-attributes and adornment with sacred noble characteristics.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 39, verse 75 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Allah has sent down the best of discourse, a Book consistent with itself, oft-repeated (mathani); the skins of those who fear their Lord shudder at it﴾ when the attributes of Majesty knock at the doors of their hearts. ﴿Then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ with longing and seeking. ﴿Allah sets forth an example: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another (mutashakisun)﴾ who pull him in different directions, and they are the concerns of the world, the concerns of dependents, and other such preoccupations. ﴿And a man belonging wholly to one man﴾ an indication of the sincere believer whom nothing has diverted from his Master, ('azza) shanuhu. ﴿So who is more wrong than one who lies against Allah﴾ this points to the state of those who falsely claim guardianship (wilaya). ﴿And denies the truth when it has come to him﴾ this points to the state of peoples who cast the Sharia behind their backs and said: it is mere husk, and we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted. ﴿On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah with their faces blackened﴾ it has been said: this is the blackness of their hearts reflected upon their faces. ﴿And those who were mindful of their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups﴾ it has been said: the righteous have worshipped Allah, Majestic is His glory, not for the sake of the Garden; so the intensity of their absorption in contemplating the dawning places of beauty and majesty prevents them from desiring the Garden, and therefore they need to be driven. It has also been said: every blameworthy or noble trait in a person drags him, without his choice, whether he wills or not, to what resembles his state, and this is the meaning of driving for both groups. It has also been said: these people are people of fidelity, so they say: "We will not enter the Garden until our beloved ones enter it," and therefore they are driven to it, but not as the unbelievers are driven. ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾ an indication that he (ﷺ) is in a seat of truth with a Sovereign Omnipotent, based on the view that the Throne does not move. ﴿Glorifying with praise their Lord﴾ an indication of their bliss. ﴿And judgment will be made between them with truth﴾ He gave each what it deserves. ﴿And it will be said: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ over the conclusion of the matter and the decisive judgment with justice, about which there is no doubt or disputation. This is it, and praise belongs to Allah the Exalted for His bounties, and blessings and peace upon His Messenger Muhammad and his family.
